structuralDecisions.decision: Add the new test as internal/intake/vocabulary_test.go in package intake (white-box, same package), not package intake_test.
structuralDecisions.rationale: It must read the unexported knownTypes/knownStatuses/knownSources/knownTrust/knownFinishes/knownAutonomies sets in vocabulary.go directly. Exporting them solely so an external test package could see them would widen the package's public API for a reason that has nothing to do with its callers.
tradeOffs: Couples the test tightly to vocabulary.go's internal representation (a map[string]bool) — acceptable here because the test's entire purpose is comparing that internal representation against two documents, not treating it as a black box.

fitness.property: vocabulary_test.go is declared `package intake` and the package still builds
fitness.verification: go build ./internal/intake/... (fails to compile if the file references unexported identifiers from a non-matching package)

structuralDecisions.decision: Decompose the comment/table parsing into small single-purpose functions (e.g. extractFieldComment, cutAtEmDash, splitPipeList, parseStatusTableColumn, assertSetsEqual) instead of one large comparison function, mirroring checkVocabulary's existing field-table style in validate.go.
structuralDecisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md's cyclomatic-complexity-<7 rule applies to every function, test code included. Six fields times (find line, cut comment, split, trim, diff) in one function would cross that budget quickly.
tradeOffs: More functions to read for the same behavior — mitigated by each one being named for exactly what it does, so no function needs a comment to explain itself.

fitness.property: Cyclomatic complexity < 7 for every function in vocabulary_test.go
fitness.verification: golangci-lint / gocyclo (the project's existing lint config) or the analyze-complexity skill, run against internal/intake/vocabulary_test.go

structuralDecisions.decision: Resolve TEMPLATE.md and README.md's paths with runtime.Caller(0) + filepath.Join(...), the same pattern TestTheShippedTemplateParses already uses in parse_test.go — no hardcoded absolute paths, no go:embed, no network or git calls.
structuralDecisions.rationale: This is the package's existing, working idiom for reaching the template from a test binary regardless of the caller's working directory. Introducing a second way to resolve the same two files would be an unforced inconsistency.
tradeOffs: Still brittle to moving templates/claude-feature-team/intake/ itself, same as the existing test — an accepted, pre-existing trade-off, not a new one this change introduces.

structuralDecisions.decision: Store the deliberately-mismatched fixture as a static file, internal/intake/testdata/mismatched_vocabulary_template.md, rather than generating it at test time with strings.Replace against the real TEMPLATE.md.
structuralDecisions.rationale: A statically committed fixture is reviewable on its own — a reader can see exactly which value was changed to disagree with vocabulary.go. A string-replace-generated fixture risks silently matching nothing (and the test passing vacuously) the moment TEMPLATE.md's wording around that field changes.
tradeOffs: The fixture can drift from TEMPLATE.md's surrounding prose over time; acceptable because the fixture's only job is to carry one field's phantom value, not to stay a faithful copy of the whole template.

fitness.property: The vocabulary-comparison check actually fails against a known-bad fixture, proving it is not a vacuous pass

structuralDecisions.decision: Treat the test's reads of templates/claude-feature-team/intake/TEMPLATE.md and README.md as local file reads of two files checked into this repository, not as a dependency on an external system requiring an interface (architecture-guardrails.md's DB/HTTP/filesystem-as-infrastructure rule does not apply here).
structuralDecisions.rationale: The files are documentation shipped in the same repo and read once per test run with no retry, timeout, or failure-mode concern — the same category as parse_test.go's existing TestTheShippedTemplateParses, which was never asked to hide its os.ReadFile behind an interface.

componentPlacement.layer: Test (same-package white-box test, not a Clean Architecture layer)
componentPlacement.reason: Needs direct access to vocabulary.go's unexported closed-vocabulary sets; sits beside check_test.go, parse_test.go, validate_test.go as another test file in the same package.
Go convention: fixtures the test binary reads but that are not Go source live in a testdata/ subdirectory, which `go build` and `go vet` both ignore by default.

crossings: templates/claude-feature-team/intake/TEMPLATE.md and README.md — documentation owned by the template directory, read (never written) by a new test in internal/intake/. No import edge is created; it is a test-time file read of plain text, identical in kind to the existing TestTheShippedTemplateParses.

layerBoundaryChecks.rule: internal/intake must not import outer-layer/framework packages (Clean Architecture dependency direction, architecture-guardrails.md #1)
layerBoundaryChecks.notes: The new test file's only imports are stdlib (os, path/filepath, runtime, strings, sort, testing) plus the intake package itself. It reads two markdown files as plain bytes via os.ReadFile — the same mechanism parse_test.go's TestTheShippedTemplateParses already uses — so no new import edge is created between internal/intake and templates/claude-feature-team/intake/. Checked by reading vocabulary.go, validate.go and parse_test.go directly; the mcp__loom__* graph tools were not invoked because this change is confined to one package and one new test file, well below the threshold where the dependency graph adds signal over a direct read. Stated here per the architect's standing instruction to say when the fallback path was used.

antiPatternChecks.notes: The three existing copies of the vocabulary (Go sets, TEMPLATE.md comments, README table) already require a three-way edit when a value changes; this feature does not fix that, it only adds a test that catches drift between them. No new shotgun-surgery edge is introduced by this change itself.
vocabulary.go stays a small set of named constants and maps; the new test does not add behavior to it, only reads it.

fitnessFunctions.property: The template's per-field comment list and the README's status table stay equal to the matching Go closed-vocabulary set
fitnessFunctions.verification: go test ./internal/intake/... (TestTemplateVocabularyMatchesGoSets, TestReadmeStatusTableMatchesGoSets) — already run by the project's existing CI test step, no new CI wiring needed

fitnessFunctions.property: The vocabulary-comparison check can actually detect a real mismatch, not just pass vacuously
fitnessFunctions.verification: go test -run TestVocabularyCheckCatchesAMismatch ./internal/intake/... against the deliberately-wrong fixture in internal/intake/testdata/mismatched_vocabulary_template.md

fitnessFunctions.property: Cyclomatic complexity < 7 for every new function introduced in vocabulary_test.go
fitnessFunctions.verification: golangci-lint / gocyclo (project's existing lint config) or the analyze-complexity skill, run against internal/intake/vocabulary_test.go

developerHandoffNotes: Declare the new file as `package intake` (same package as vocabulary.go), not `intake_test` — it needs direct access to knownTypes/knownStatuses/knownSources/knownTrust/knownFinishes/knownAutonomies.

Reuse validate.go's existing field-table idiom: a slice of {name, extracted-values, allowed-set} structs iterated once, mirroring checkVocabulary — this keeps both TestTemplateVocabularyMatchesGoSets and TestReadmeStatusTableMatchesGoSets table-driven and short.

Split parsing into named helpers (extractFieldComment, cutAtEmDash, splitPipeList, parseStatusTableColumn, assertSetsEqual) so no single function approaches the complexity-7 ceiling; assertSetsEqual should be the one place that produces the 'field X, document Y, missing on side Z' failure message, shared by both the TEMPLATE.md and README.md checks.

Resolve both file paths the same way TestTheShippedTemplateParses does in parse_test.go: runtime.Caller(0) + filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(here), "..", "..", "templates", "claude-feature-team", "intake", "TEMPLATE.md"/"README.md").
AC4 requires failing loudly, never silently passing, when a field's comment can't be found or parsed — use t.Fatalf naming the field, not a skipped subtest or a swallowed error.

internal/intake/testdata/mismatched_vocabulary_template.md should be a static copy of TEMPLATE.md with exactly one field's trailing comment edited to disagree with its Go set (e.g. add a phantom status `queued`); do not generate it at test time.
No file outside internal/intake/ should change except this run's own delivery record under docs/features/i-4-vocabulary-test/ — confirm with git status before finishing (AC6).

The analyst flagged this and deferred it: the spec's AC6 restricts file changes to internal/intake/ plus the delivery record, so this architecture leaves DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md untouched for this feature.
